newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Singapore trader buys more diesel.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Singapore trader buys more diesel.

text.p: Singapore's gas oil market remained dominated by a local trader who bought another 520,000 million barrels, bringing its purchase to a staggering total of nearly eight million barrels so far, traders said on Friday.
The trader's purchases sustained both physical and swaps prices at firm levels.

The cargoes for end-April/early May were done around $26.70-$26.90 per barrel free-on-board (fob), while earlier dates were traded at $27.30. Sellers were a European major, a Swiss trader and a Dutch trader.
The jet fuel market was quiet with an offer from a Chinese trader at $26.40 per barrel fob, higher than its sale on Thursday at $25.90.

Interest was focused on India's kerosene import tender for May delivery with low offers seen at $1.70 per tonne above MidEast spot quotes, and $34.90-$35.00 per tonne above the high of Mediterranean quotes, both on a c-and-f Indian east coast basis.

Traders said the $1.70-premium reflected current fob premium levels in the MidEast spot quotes which is at parity. Front runners in the Indian tender, which would be awarded this evening, were made by a European major, a US major and a Mediterranean trader, said traders.
The market was hoping that India would provide some support to soft jet fuel prices.

Traders also said that after the large 1.175-million-barrel draw in middle-distillate stocks in the week ended April 2, storage tanks in Singapore are expected to be filled up again for the rest of April.
They said most of the tank space have already been fully booked, attributing this to the large arbitrage cargoes which are coming to this region.
